page.layout: One page of verse, centred block of lines; page number and running head at top; catchword-like word "Obliuioso" at lower right under the last line. Faint show-through of the facing page on the right edge (not transcribed).

main_text.p: Dulceis sonora magnanimis Ducum Coeptis nocebunt: nec frementes Docta tubas animare Musa. Quum corda vellit grandia fortium. Quum mentis alta promouet impetus: Et laude clarorum perenni Facta virûm decoranda saeclis Tollit futuris. Non Phariae suos Ornant Tyrannos pyramides magis. Non sculpta Mausolea sumptu Magnifico monimenta Carum Regem celebrant. Non magis aethere Pendentium alto magna Semiramin Commendat hortorum, aut sepulchri Structa viro Babylone moles. Charas Auorum tristis imagines Delet vetustas, aeraque fortior Antiqua, caelatosque vultus Dente terit Caries superbo: Imbresve nymbis qui gelidi ruunt: Aut quos Rubentis robore brachij Commotus ignes Rex suprema Caelituum iaculatur arce. Attrita tandem marmora concidunt, Arcusque celsis nubibus aemuli. Hac cuncta Saturnus resecta Falce truci violentus aufert. Quos funeranit liuida mors statim

page.notes: Verse set in italic throughout; the last line "Quos funeranit liuida mors statim" and the word "Obliuioso" at lower right are as printed (the catchword is the signature-line word in the right corner). Some letters in the italic are doubtful, notably "Charas", "Pendentium", and "Carum"; the long s is printed as f in places in the source and is rendered here as s.
